en.title: Set System vs Cumulative Score Match Formats
en.excerpt: Comprehensive explanation of World Archery match play scoring: the Set System used for Recurve/Barebow vs the Cumulative Score System used for Compound.
en.content:
Two Elimination Scoring Philosophies

World Archery defines two distinct scoring mechanisms for individual elimination matches. Choosing the correct format ensures your tournament follows sanctioned rules.

The Set System (Recurve & Barebow)

Individual Recurve and Barebow matches use the Set System:

  • Each match consists of up to 5 sets. In each set, archers shoot 3 arrows (maximum 30 points).
  • The archer with the higher score in a set receives 2 set points.
  • If the scores are tied in a set, both archers receive 1 set point each.
  • The first archer to reach 6 set points wins the match.
  • If tied 5-5 after 5 sets, a one-arrow shoot-off is conducted.

Cumulative Score System (Compound)

Compound matches use the Cumulative Score System:

  • Archers shoot 5 ends of 3 arrows (15 arrows total, maximum 150 points).
  • Scores are added cumulatively throughout the match without set points.
  • The archer with the highest total score after 15 arrows wins the match.
  • If total scores are tied after 5 ends, a one-arrow shoot-off is conducted.

Configuring Formats in Archeris

When creating a category in Archeris, select Recurve Set System or Compound Cumulative. The scorekeeper mobile interface automatically switches its calculation engine to match the chosen format.
